# 0. Packages

```{r packages}
# The packages this analysis needs. Any that are missing are installed from
# CRAN the first time you knit (this can take a few minutes, once).
pkgs <- c("quanteda", "quanteda.textstats", "seededlda", "stopwords",
          "tidyverse", "stringi", "Rtsne", "plotly", "LDAvis", "knitr", "jsonlite",
          "clue", "ggrepel", "ragg")
missing <- setdiff(pkgs, rownames(installed.packages()))
if (length(missing)) install.packages(missing, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")

library(quanteda)            # tokenizing and document-feature matrices
library(quanteda.textstats)  # keyness (collocates)
library(seededlda)           # unsupervised and seeded LDA
library(stopwords)           # the marimo Chinese stopword list
library(tidyverse)           # data cleaning (dplyr, stringr, readr, ggplot2...)
library(stringi)             # traditional -> simplified conversion
library(Rtsne)               # t-SNE
library(plotly)              # interactive t-SNE plots
library(LDAvis)              # interactive topic map
library(knitr)               # kable() tables
library(ggrepel)             # non-overlapping word labels in the static t-SNE figures
# (ragg, used to save the figures as PNG with Chinese text, is called as ragg::)
# (clue is used below to match topics between runs; it is called as clue::)

# Folder for all outputs: one new folder per run, named by date and time, inside
# r_output/ (e.g. r_output/run_2026-10-17_0930/). Earlier runs are never overwritten.
out_dir <- file.path("r_output", paste0("run_", format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d_%H%M")))
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
cat("All outputs of this run are saved in:", out_dir, "\n")
# Keep a copy of this Rmd with the outputs, so each run records the code that made it
if (!is.null(knitr::current_input())) {
  file.copy(knitr::current_input(), out_dir, overwrite = TRUE)
}
# All CSVs are saved with write_excel_csv(): it adds a marker at the start of the
# file so Excel opens the Chinese text correctly instead of showing garbled text.
```

# 1. Load and clean

Long reviews: title and text are combined (the 2026 scraper stores the title
separately; for example, one review's title is "真是克夫"). Five reviews that
the same author posted twice are removed.

Short comments: the one empty comment is dropped, and Douban's edit stamps
("@2016-10-27 10:00:54") are stripped.

Both corpora are converted from traditional to simplified characters, and the
heroine's name is unified (陈树娟 / 淑娟 → 树娟) so that every mention counts
as the same word.

```{r load}
# Convert traditional characters to simplified (some reviews are in 繁体).
# If the converter is unavailable on this computer, the text is left unchanged.
to_simplified <- function(x) {
  tryCatch(stri_trans_general(x, "Traditional-Simplified"), error = function(e) x)
}

# One cleaning function applied to every text:
#  - empty values become ""
#  - traditional -> simplified
#  - remove Douban's "@2016-10-27 10:00:54" edit stamps
#  - unify the heroine's name (陈树娟 and the common misspelling 淑娟 -> 树娟)
#  - unify Zhu Ying's name (朱英 -> 朱瑛)
#  - unify the Cultural Revolution (文化大革命 -> 文革), so every mention reaches
#    the seed word 文革 and is not split into 文化 / 大 / 革命
normalize <- function(x) {
  x %>%
    replace_na("") %>%
    to_simplified() %>%
    str_replace_all("@\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2} \\d{2}:\\d{2}:\\d{2}", "") %>%
    str_replace_all("陈树娟|淑娟", "树娟") %>%
    str_replace_all("朱英", "朱瑛") %>%
    str_replace_all("文化大革命", "文革")
}

# --- Long reviews (影评) ---
long_raw <- read_csv("reviews_1303967/reviews_unique.csv",
                     col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))

long <- long_raw %>%
  distinct(text, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%                      # drop the 5 double posts
  mutate(text_full = normalize(paste(title, text, sep = "\n")),  # title + body
         date = ymd_hms(str_sub(date, 1, 19), quiet = TRUE),
         year = year(date),
         rating = as.numeric(rating),
         useful = as.numeric(useful),
         corpus = "long") %>%
  select(id = rid, author = author_hash, date, year, rating,
         votes = useful, text = text_full, corpus)

# --- Short comments (短评) ---
short_raw <- read_csv("blue_kite_douban_unique.csv",
                      col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))

short <- short_raw %>%
  filter(!is.na(text), str_trim(text) != "") %>%            # drop the empty comment
  mutate(text = normalize(text),
         date = ymd_hms(str_sub(date, 1, 19), quiet = TRUE),
         year = year(date),
         rating = as.numeric(rating),
         votes = as.numeric(votes),
         corpus = "short") %>%
  select(id = cid, author = user_hash, date, year, rating, votes, text, corpus,
         starts_with("in_"))                                 # which Douban lists it was in

# Both corpora in one table (used for counts and the 克夫 export)
both <- bind_rows(long, short)
```

```{r summary}
# Numbers for the methods section: documents, distinct authors, date range, length.
corpus_summary <- both %>%
  group_by(corpus) %>%

            first = min(date, na.rm = TRUE),

            total_chars = sum(nchar(text)))
kable(corpus_summary)
cat("Distinct authors across both corpora:",
    n_distinct(both$author[!is.na(both$author) & both$author != ""]), "\n")
write_excel_csv(corpus_summary, file.path(out_dir, "corpus_summary.csv"))
```

# 2. Tokenization and stopwords

quanteda splits Chinese with ICU's dictionary, which breaks many names and
some key words into single characters (树娟 → 树 | 娟, 田壮壮 → 田 | 壮 | 壮,
霸王别姬 → 霸王 | 别 | 姬, 禁片 → 禁 | 片). The `compounds` list joins them
back. This matters: without it, the model never sees 树娟 as a word.

```{r split-demo}
# Demonstration of the problem: how quanteda splits these phrases on its own
tokens(c("树娟的命运", "田壮壮的禁片", "霸王别姬和活着"))
```

```{r tokenize}
# Names and words that the tokenizer breaks apart; they are glued back together.
compounds <- c("田壮壮", "树娟", "吕丽萍", "林少龙", "少龙", "李国栋", "国栋",
               "濮存昕", "李雪健", "郭宝昌", "陈树生", "树生", "朱瑛",
               "张艺谋", "陈凯歌", "霸王别姬", "禁片", "被禁", "禁拍", "反右",
               "反思", "劳改", "文工团", "第五代", "吴清源", "蓝风筝",
               "男权", "女权", "母爱", "女主角", "女主")

# Base stopword list: marimo Chinese stopwords (same as the CulturaCognize pipeline)
base_stop <- tryCatch(stopwords("zh", source = "marimo"),
                      error = function(e) stopwords("zh", source = "misc"))

# Custom stopword list, built from the most frequent tokens in
# this corpus that carry no content (filler, platform and generic film words).
# Character names, the director, and comparison films are deliberately KEPT.
custom_stop <- c(
  # generic film / platform words
  "电影", "影片", "片子", "本片", "全片", "片中", "一部", "这部", "影评", "看过",
  "看完", "看了", "蓝风筝", "风筝",
  # filler and function words not in marimo
  "一个", "没有", "自己", "就是", "他们", "都是", "时候", "的是", "可以", "人的",
  "一种", "觉得", "一样", "感觉", "也是", "看到", "出来", "开始", "中的", "其实",
  "不能", "这种", "还有", "现在", "知道", "怎么", "已经", "一直", "真的",
  "不知道", "虽然", "一段", "甚至", "只能", "一次", "并不", "可是", "也许",
  "只有", "后来", "一点", "就像", "成了", "比较", "有些", "有点", "起来",
  "比如", "总是", "本身", "来说", "有人", "能够", "整个", "我想", "一般",
  "终于", "需要", "太多", "大家", "真正", "除了", "一句", "那种", "不够",
  "特别", "不会", "的话", "同时", "或许", "好像", "当然", "很好", "这里",
  "到了", "告诉", "无论", "都有", "不想", "上了", "不要", "更加", "一起",
  "最后", "很多", "事情", "东西", "一些", "这样", "那样", "这么", "那么",
  # added after reviewing the exploratory results (t-SNE, unsupervised LDA):
  # filler words that carried no content in clusters or topics
  "之后", "无法", "应该", "可能", "发生", "出现", "似乎", "成为", "喜欢", "非常",
  "一下", "最终",
  # possessives (pure grammar; some slipped past the base list)
  "我的", "你的", "他的", "她的", "它的", "我们的", "他们的", "她们的",
  # the suffix of 历史性的 / 悲剧性的 cut off by the tokenizer
  # (it means "-ic / -al", not gender or sex)
  "性的")

# Single characters are dropped (mostly particles like 了 着 被), except these,
# which carry meaning in this corpus.
keep_single <- c("嫁", "命", "死", "家", "爱", "党", "苦", "惨", "恨", "痛", "禁")

# The full tokenizing recipe, applied the same way to every corpus:
#  1. split into words, dropping punctuation, numbers, symbols and links
#  2. glue the split names back together (compounds)
#  3. lowercase (for the few English words)
#  4. remove Chinese and English stopwords
#  5. keep words of 2+ characters, plus the meaningful single characters
prep_tokens <- function(corp) {
  tokens(corp, remove_punct = TRUE, remove_numbers = TRUE,
         remove_symbols = TRUE, remove_url = TRUE) %>%
    tokens_compound(pattern = as.list(tokens(compounds)), concatenator = "") %>%
    tokens_tolower() %>%
    tokens_remove(pattern = c(base_stop, custom_stop, stopwords("en"))) %>%
    tokens_keep(pattern = c("^.{2,}$", paste0("^", keep_single, "$")),
                valuetype = "regex")
}

# Save the full stopword list (for the paper's appendix)
writeLines(c("# marimo zh (base)", base_stop, "", "# custom", custom_stop,
             "", "# single characters kept", keep_single),
           file.path(out_dir, "stopwords_used.txt"))
```

```{r tokens-check}
# Sanity check: each key word should appear about as often as a token as it does
# in the raw text. A big gap would mean the tokenizer is still splitting it.
corp_long <- corpus(long, docid_field = "id", text_field = "text")
toks_long <- prep_tokens(corp_long)
key_words <- c("树娟", "吕丽萍", "母亲", "妈妈", "女人", "克夫", "田壮壮",
               "霸王别姬", "活着", "禁片", "反右")
kable(tibble(word = key_words,
             tokens = sapply(key_words, function(w) sum(ntoken(tokens_keep(toks_long, w)))),
             raw_string = sapply(key_words, function(w) sum(str_count(long$text, fixed(w))))))
```

# 3. What viewers mention: counts

Share of texts in each corpus that mention at least one word in a group
(string matching on the cleaned text, so tokenization does not matter here).
Short comments are far shorter (median about 20 characters versus about 600),
so compare **within** each corpus, for example each group relative to history,
rather than raw percentages across corpora.

```{r counts}
# Word groups to count. "|" means "or": a text counts if it contains any of them.
groups <- list(
  history          = "历史|时代|年代",
  campaigns        = "文革|文化大革命|反右|右派|大跃进|红卫兵|批斗|整风",
  ban              = "禁片|被禁|禁拍|禁映|封禁",
  film_comparison  = "活着|霸王别姬",
  director         = "田壮壮|导演",
  mother_shujuan   = "母亲|妈妈|树娟|吕丽萍|女主",
  fathers          = "父亲|爸爸|继父|叔叔",
  child_tietou     = "铁头|孩子|儿子|童年",
  marriage         = "婚姻|结婚|改嫁|嫁|丈夫|寡妇",
  women_gender     = "女人|女性|妇女|性别|男权|女权|父权",
  kefu             = "克夫",
  fate             = "命运|命苦|宿命"
)

# For each group and corpus: how many texts mention it, the share of texts,
# and how many per 100 texts that mention history (a length-neutral comparison).
counts <- map_dfr(names(groups), function(g) {
  both %>%
    group_by(corpus) %>%
    summarise(n_docs = n(), n_mention = sum(str_detect(text, groups[[g]]))) %>%
    mutate(group = g)
}) %>%
  mutate(share = round(100 * n_mention / n_docs, 1)) %>%
  group_by(corpus) %>%
  mutate(per_100_history = round(100 * n_mention / n_mention[group == "history"], 0)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(group, corpus, n_mention, n_docs, share, per_100_history) %>%
  arrange(factor(group, levels = names(groups)), corpus)

kable(counts)
write_excel_csv(counts, file.path(out_dir, "counts_by_group.csv"))
```

# 4. Collocates: which words surround the mother, women, and 克夫?

Keyness of words within 10 tokens of each target, compared with the rest of
the long reviews (chi-squared; Watanabe's target-word collocation method).

```{r collocates}
# For a target word: compare the words within 10 tokens of it ("inside") with
# all other words ("outside"). Words much more common inside are its collocates.
collocates <- function(toks, target, window = 10, n = 20) {
  inside  <- tokens_keep(toks, pattern = target, window = window) %>%
    tokens_remove(pattern = target)                      # don't count the target itself
  outside <- tokens_remove(toks, pattern = target, window = window)
  if (sum(ntoken(inside)) == 0) return(tibble())
  key <- textstat_keyness(rbind(dfm(inside), dfm(outside)),
                          target = seq_len(ndoc(inside)))
  key %>% as_tibble() %>% filter(n_target >= 3) %>% head(n)  # at least 3 co-occurrences
}

# The targets (several words count as one target, e.g. all mother words)
targets <- list(mother = c("母亲", "妈妈", "树娟", "吕丽萍"),
                women  = c("女人", "女性", "妇女"),
                kefu   = "克夫",
                history = "历史")

coll <- map(targets, ~ collocates(toks_long, .x))
for (nm in names(coll)) {
  cat("\n###", nm, "\n")
  print(kable(coll[[nm]] %>% select(feature, chi2, p, n_target, n_reference)))
}
bind_rows(coll, .id = "target") %>% write_excel_csv(file.path(out_dir, "collocates_long.csv"))
```

# 5. 克夫 texts for hand-coding

Every long review and short comment that uses 克夫, with the passage around
the word. Code each one in the `code` column:

- **A** applies the label to Shujuan (seriously or as a joke)
- **R** rejects the label or blames the era instead
- **Q** raises the question without deciding (her fate or the era?)
- **M** meta comment (about other viewers, the script, or the label itself)
- **O** other

```{r kefu}
# Every text containing 克夫, with 60 characters on each side of the word,
# and empty columns to fill in by hand. Sorted by corpus, then by votes.
kefu <- both %>%
  filter(str_detect(text, "克夫")) %>%
  mutate(pos = str_locate(text, "克夫")[, 1],
         context = str_sub(text, pmax(1, pos - 60), pos + 61),
         code = "", notes = "") %>%
  arrange(corpus, desc(votes)) %>%
  select(corpus, id, date, rating, votes, context, code, notes, text)

cat(nrow(kefu), "texts mention 克夫 (", sum(kefu$corpus == "long"), "long,",
    sum(kefu$corpus == "short"), "short )\n")
# write_excel_csv adds a marker so Excel opens the Chinese text correctly.
# NOTE: re-knitting overwrites this file, so save your coded copy under a new name.
write_excel_csv(kefu, file.path(out_dir, "kefu_for_coding.csv"))
```

# 6. Modeling corpus: long reviews split into paragraphs

306 long reviews are too few documents for stable topic models, so each review
is split into paragraphs, following common practice for long texts (Jockers
2013; Schöch 2017). Paragraphs under 30 characters (titles, one-liners) are
attached to the paragraph that follows. Results are checked at the review
level in section 11.

```{r paragraphs}
# Split each review at line breaks, then merge short pieces (< 30 characters,
# e.g. titles) into the next paragraph so no document is nearly empty.
paras <- long %>%
  mutate(p = str_split(text, "\n+")) %>%
  select(id, date, year, rating, votes, p) %>%
  unnest(p) %>%
  mutate(p = str_trim(p)) %>%
  filter(p != "") %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  # a new chunk starts after every paragraph of 30+ characters
  mutate(chunk = cumsum(lag(nchar(p) >= 30, default = FALSE))) %>%
  group_by(id, date, year, rating, votes, chunk) %>%
  summarise(text = paste(p, collapse = "\n"), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(doc_id = paste0(id, "_", chunk))

corp_para <- corpus(paras, docid_field = "doc_id", text_field = "text")
toks_para <- prep_tokens(corp_para)

# Document-feature matrix: keep words used at least 5 times in at least 3 paragraphs
dfmat <- dfm(toks_para) %>%
  dfm_trim(min_termfreq = 5, min_docfreq = 3)
dfmat <- dfm_subset(dfmat, ntoken(dfmat) > 0)        # drop paragraphs left empty

cat("Paragraph documents:", ndoc(dfmat), " Vocabulary:", nfeat(dfmat), "\n")
topfeatures(dfmat, 40)
```

# 7. Exploratory t-SNE

Each dot is a word. Words used in the same paragraphs sit close together.
Colors are k-means clusters of the dots, computed separately for each plot,
so cluster numbers do not correspond between the two plots. Nearness *within*
a cluster is meaningful; distances *between* clusters are not.

```{r tsne-function}
# Build a t-SNE map of the given word-by-paragraph matrix, color it by 5 k-means
# clusters, and return an interactive plot with its own title and legend.
tsne_plot <- function(m, title, seed, out_csv = NULL) {
  set.seed(seed)                                      # same layout every knit
  m <- m[!duplicated(m), ]                            # t-SNE cannot take duplicate rows
  ts <- Rtsne(m, dims = 2, perplexity = 20, check_duplicates = FALSE)
  df <- tibble(Dim1 = ts$Y[, 1], Dim2 = ts$Y[, 2], Term = rownames(m))
  df$Cluster <- as.factor(kmeans(df[, 1:2], centers = 5)$cluster)
  # Save each word's cluster (for the cluster tables), strongest words first
  if (!is.null(out_csv)) {
    df %>% mutate(weight = rowSums(m)) %>% arrange(Cluster, desc(weight)) %>%
      write_excel_csv(out_csv)
  }
  plot_ly(df, x = ~Dim1, y = ~Dim2, type = "scatter", mode = "markers+text",
          color = ~Cluster, text = ~Term, textposition = "top center",
          marker = list(size = 8)) %>%
    # margin t = 70 leaves room above the plot so the title is not clipped
    layout(title = list(text = title, y = 0.98, yanchor = "top"),
           margin = list(t = 70),
           legend = list(title = list(text = "cluster"))) %>%
    # the camera icon on the plot saves a sharp PNG (2x resolution)
    config(toImageButtonOptions = list(format = "png", width = 1100,
                                       height = 850, scale = 2))
}
```

## Frequency-based: the most common words

```{r tsne-freq, fig.width=9, fig.height=7}
# Rows = the 80 most frequent words; columns = their counts in each paragraph
term_freq <- t(as.matrix(dfmat))
top_freq <- names(sort(rowSums(term_freq), decreasing = TRUE))[1:80]
tsne_plot(term_freq[top_freq, ], "t-SNE: top 80 terms by frequency", 1,
          out_csv = file.path(out_dir, "tsne_freq_clusters.csv"))
```

## TF-IDF-based: the most distinctive words

```{r tsne-tfidf, fig.width=9, fig.height=7}
# TF-IDF down-weights words that appear everywhere, so distinctive words rise
term_tfidf <- t(as.matrix(dfm_tfidf(dfmat)))
top_tfidf <- names(sort(rowMeans(term_tfidf), decreasing = TRUE))[1:80]
tsne_plot(term_tfidf[top_tfidf, ], "t-SNE: top 80 terms by TF-IDF", 2,
          out_csv = file.path(out_dir, "tsne_tfidf_clusters.csv"))
```

## Static figures for the paper

The interactive maps above are for exploring. This chunk draws print-ready
versions and saves them as 300-dpi PNGs (`fig_tsne_freq.png` and
`fig_tsne_tfidf.png` in this run's folder) to paste into the paper. They are drawn from the
saved cluster CSVs, so the layout and clusters are exactly the same as above
and in the cluster tables. Labels are pushed apart so they do not overlap.
Set `show_titles` to FALSE to drop the titles inside the images (in the paper
the title can go in the figure caption instead).

To show cluster names instead of numbers, fill in `freq_names` and
`tfidf_names` and rerun **this chunk only** (no need to rerun the t-SNE).
`label_lang` switches the word labels between English, Chinese, or both.

```{r tsne-static, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=4.4, dev="ragg_png"}
# A Chinese font that exists on this computer (the first one found is used)
fig_font <- intersect(c("PingFang SC", "Hiragino Sans GB", "Songti SC", "STHeiti"),
                      systemfonts::system_fonts()$family)[1]
if (is.na(fig_font)) fig_font <- ""   # none found: R's default font
cat("Font for the figures:", fig_font, "\n")

# Cluster names: leave as NULL to show numbers, or fill in like this
# (the number on the left must match the cluster number in the CSV):
# freq_names <- c("1" = "Shujuan and her husbands", "2" = "...", "3" = "...",
#                 "4" = "...", "5" = "...")
freq_names  <- NULL
tfidf_names <- NULL

# Word labels: "en" = English, "zh" = Chinese, "both" = Chinese above English.
# English comes from tsne_glossary.csv (same translations as the cluster table;
# edit that file to change a translation). Words missing from it stay in Chinese.
label_lang <- "en"

# Titles inside the images (TRUE) or none (FALSE)
show_titles <- FALSE   # ASA style: the title goes in the figure caption
gloss <- read_csv("tsne_glossary.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

tsne_static <- function(csv, names, out_png, title = NULL) {
  df <- read_csv(csv, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(Cluster = as.character(Cluster)) %>%
    left_join(gloss, by = "Term") %>%
    mutate(label = case_when(label_lang == "zh" | is.na(English) ~ Term,
                             label_lang == "en" ~ English,
                             TRUE ~ paste0(Term, "\n", English)))
  if (any(is.na(df$English))) {
    cat("No English in tsne_glossary.csv for:", df$Term[is.na(df$English)], "\n")
  }
  if (!is.null(names)) {
    df$Cluster <- factor(names[df$Cluster], levels = names)
  }
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(Dim1, Dim2, color = Cluster, shape = Cluster)) +
    geom_point(size = 1.8) +
    geom_text_repel(aes(label = label), family = fig_font,
                    size = if (label_lang == "both") 2.6 else 3, lineheight = 0.9,
                    max.overlaps = Inf,          # show every word
                    box.padding = 0.25, point.padding = 0.15,
                    min.segment.length = 0.3, segment.size = 0.2,
                    seed = 1, show.legend = FALSE) +
    # colors plus shapes, so clusters stay distinct in black-and-white print
    scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2", name = "Cluster") +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 17, 15, 18, 8), name = "Cluster") +
    labs(title = if (show_titles) title else NULL,
         x = "t-SNE dimension 1", y = "t-SNE dimension 2") +
    theme_minimal(base_family = fig_font, base_size = 10) +
    theme(legend.position = "right",        # legend beside the map, so the figure is wide, not square
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
  ggsave(out_png, p, width = 7.5, height = 4.4, dpi = 300,
         device = ragg::agg_png, bg = "white")
  p
}

tsne_static(file.path(out_dir, "tsne_freq_clusters.csv"),  freq_names,  file.path(out_dir, "fig_tsne_freq.png"),
            title = "The 80 most frequent words")
tsne_static(file.path(out_dir, "tsne_tfidf_clusters.csv"), tfidf_names, file.path(out_dir, "fig_tsne_tfidf.png"),
            title = "The 80 most distinctive words (TF-IDF)")
```

# 8. Unsupervised LDA

```{r helpers}
# Two helper functions used by the models below.

# topic_share(): share of all words in the corpus assigned to each topic
topic_share <- function(m, x = dfmat) {
  doc_len <- rowSums(x)
  sort(colSums(m$theta * doc_len) / sum(doc_len), decreasing = TRUE)
}

# landing(): for each word, which topic it most likely belongs to, and how strongly.
# p(topic | word) = p(word | topic) x topic size, normalized over topics.
landing <- function(m, words, x = dfmat) {
  sizes <- colSums(m$theta * rowSums(x))             # how big each topic is
  words <- intersect(words, colnames(m$phi))
  map_dfr(words, function(w) {
    p <- m$phi[, w] * sizes
    p <- p / sum(p)
    tibble(word = w, top_topic = names(which.max(p)),
           p_top = round(max(p), 2),
           second = names(sort(p, decreasing = TRUE))[2],
           p_second = round(sort(p, decreasing = TRUE)[2], 2))
  })
}

# ---- Comparing runs of the same model (to pick the most typical run) ----
cosine <- function(a, b) sum(a * b) / sqrt(sum(a^2) * sum(b^2))
js_div <- function(p, q) {                    # Jensen-Shannon divergence (LDAvis's distance)
  m <- (p + q) / 2
  0.5 * sum(p * log(p / m)) + 0.5 * sum(q * log(q / m))
}

# Pair up the topics of two runs. Seeded runs: topics with the same name.
# Unsupervised runs (no names): optimal one-to-one matching on word similarity.
pair_topics <- function(m1, m2, names = NULL) {
  if (!is.null(names)) {
    return(list(i1 = match(names, rownames(m1$phi)), i2 = match(names, rownames(m2$phi))))
  }
  A <- m1$phi; B <- m2$phi
  S <- (A %*% t(B)) / outer(sqrt(rowSums(A^2)), sqrt(rowSums(B^2)))
  if (requireNamespace("clue", quietly = TRUE)) {
    perm <- as.integer(clue::solve_LSAP(S, maximum = TRUE))
  } else {                                    # greedy matching if clue is missing
    perm <- integer(nrow(S))
    for (r in seq_len(nrow(S))) {
      idx <- which(S == max(S), arr.ind = TRUE)[1, ]
      perm[idx[1]] <- idx[2]; S[idx[1], ] <- -Inf; S[, idx[2]] <- -Inf
    }
  }
  list(i1 = seq_len(nrow(A)), i2 = perm)
}

# Four ways two runs can agree (1 = identical):
#   words     - matched topics have the same word distributions (cosine similarity)
#   sizes     - topics take up the same share of the corpus (1 - total variation distance)
#   documents - the same paragraphs are assigned to the same topics (correlation of theta)
#   distances - topics sit in the same positions relative to each other, i.e. the
#               LDAvis map (correlation of the topic-to-topic distance matrices)
compare_two <- function(m1, m2, names = NULL, x = dfmat) {
  pr <- pair_topics(m1, m2, names); i1 <- pr$i1; i2 <- pr$i2
  len <- rowSums(x)
  s1 <- colSums(m1$theta * len) / sum(len)
  s2 <- colSums(m2$theta * len) / sum(len)
  d1 <- outer(i1, i1, Vectorize(function(a, b) js_div(m1$phi[a, ], m1$phi[b, ])))
  d2 <- outer(i2, i2, Vectorize(function(a, b) js_div(m2$phi[a, ], m2$phi[b, ])))
  c(words     = mean(mapply(function(a, b) cosine(m1$phi[a, ], m2$phi[b, ]), i1, i2)),
    sizes     = 1 - 0.5 * sum(abs(s1[i1] - s2[i2])),
    documents = mean(mapply(function(a, b) cor(m1$theta[, a], m2$theta[, b]), i1, i2)),
    distances = cor(d1[upper.tri(d1)], d2[upper.tri(d2)]))
}

# Compare every pair of runs. For each criterion, each run's average agreement
# with all other runs is ranked (1 = most typical); the most typical run overall
# has the best average rank across the four criteria.
typical_run <- function(runs, names = NULL, x = dfmat) {
  n <- length(runs); crit <- c("words", "sizes", "documents", "distances")
  sims <- array(NA, c(n, n, 4), dimnames = list(NULL, NULL, crit))
  for (i in 1:(n - 1)) for (j in (i + 1):n) {
    v <- compare_two(runs[[i]], runs[[j]], names, x)
    sims[i, j, ] <- v
    sims[j, i, ] <- v
  }
  avg <- apply(sims, c(1, 3), mean, na.rm = TRUE)          # runs x criteria
  ranks <- apply(-avg, 2, rank)                            # 1 = most typical
  tab <- bind_cols(tibble(run_seed = seq_len(n)), as_tibble(round(avg, 3))) %>%
    mutate(mean_rank = rowMeans(ranks)) %>%
    arrange(mean_rank)
  overall <- t(apply(sims, 3, function(m) c(mean = mean(m, na.rm = TRUE),
                                            min = min(m, na.rm = TRUE),
                                            max = max(m, na.rm = TRUE))))
  list(medoid = tab$run_seed[1], table = tab, overall = round(overall, 3))
}

# Per-topic stability: for each topic of the most typical run, how closely does
# its matching topic in each other run resemble it? Strong, central themes come
# back almost unchanged; small or fuzzy themes vary. Only interpret stable topics.
# (0.8 is a rule-of-thumb cutoff for "essentially the same topic".)
topic_stability <- function(runs, medoid, names = NULL) {
  ref <- runs[[medoid]]
  others <- setdiff(seq_along(runs), medoid)
  sims <- sapply(others, function(r) {
    pr <- pair_topics(ref, runs[[r]], names)
    mapply(function(a, b) cosine(ref$phi[a, ], runs[[r]]$phi[b, ]), pr$i1, pr$i2)
  })                                                # topics x other runs
  if (is.null(dim(sims))) sims <- matrix(sims, nrow = 1)
  ids <- if (is.null(names)) seq_len(nrow(ref$phi)) else match(names, rownames(ref$phi))
  tops <- apply(seededlda::terms(ref, 6), 2, paste, collapse = " ")
  tibble(topic = rownames(ref$phi)[ids],
         top_words = tops[ids],
         mean_similarity = round(rowMeans(sims), 3),
         pct_runs_above_0.8 = round(100 * rowMeans(sims >= 0.8)))
}
```

## Choosing the number of topics (k)

The model is fitted for several values of k and two measures are compared:

- **Perplexity** (lower is better fit). On the data the model was trained on,
  it almost always keeps falling as k grows, so it cannot pick k alone; look
  for where the curve flattens.
- **Divergence** (higher means topics are more distinct from each other;
  Watanabe and Baturo's measure in seededlda). Look for where it peaks or
  stops rising.

A second set of standard measures comes from the `ldatuning` package
(Griffiths & Steyvers 2004; Cao Juan et al. 2009; Arun et al. 2010; Deveaud
et al. 2014). Then read the top words for the candidate values: the final
choice should also give interpretable topics (Chang et al. 2009 show that
better statistical fit does not guarantee more interpretable topics). Finally,
check whether the substantive findings hold across the whole sensible range.

```{r k-test, fig.width=9, fig.height=4}
# Safely compute a seededlda fit measure (returns NA if this version lacks it)
metric <- function(fname, m) {
  if (!exists(fname, envir = asNamespace("seededlda"))) return(NA_real_)
  tryCatch(as.numeric(get(fname, envir = asNamespace("seededlda"))(m)),
           error = function(e) NA_real_)
}

k_values <- c(4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 15)
k_models <- list()
k_test <- map_dfr(k_values, function(k) {
  set.seed(2024)
  m <- textmodel_lda(dfmat, k = k, max_iter = 2000, auto_iter = TRUE)
  k_models[[as.character(k)]] <<- m                 # keep each model for section below
  tibble(k = k,
         perplexity = metric("perplexity", m),
         divergence = metric("divergence", m))
})
kable(k_test)
write_excel_csv(k_test, file.path(out_dir, "k_selection.csv"))

# Plot both measures against k
k_test %>%
  pivot_longer(-k, names_to = "measure") %>%
  ggplot(aes(k, value)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~ measure, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = k_values) +
  labs(title = "Unsupervised LDA: fit by number of topics", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## ldatuning: four standard measures

```{r ldatuning, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
# ldatuning fits a standard LDA (topicmodels package) at each k and reports:
#   Griffiths2004 (maximize), Deveaud2014 (maximize),
#   CaoJuan2009 (minimize), Arun2010 (minimize).
# Look for the k where the "maximize" lines peak and the "minimize" lines bottom out.
# This is the slowest chunk (a few minutes). If the packages cannot be installed,
# it is skipped and the rest of the report still knits.
tuning_pkgs <- c("ldatuning", "topicmodels")
need <- setdiff(tuning_pkgs, rownames(installed.packages()))
if (length(need)) try(install.packages(need, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org"))

if (all(sapply(tuning_pkgs, requireNamespace, quietly = TRUE))) {
  dtm <- convert(dfmat, to = "topicmodels")          # quanteda dfm -> topicmodels format
  tuning <- ldatuning::FindTopicsNumber(
    dtm, topics = k_values,
    metrics = c("Griffiths2004", "CaoJuan2009", "Arun2010", "Deveaud2014"),
    method = "Gibbs", control = list(seed = 2024), mc.cores = 2L, verbose = FALSE)
  print(kable(tuning))
  write_excel_csv(tuning, file.path(out_dir, "k_selection_ldatuning.csv"))
  ldatuning::FindTopicsNumber_plot(tuning)
} else {
  cat("ldatuning or topicmodels could not be installed; this check was skipped.\n")
}
```

## Do the findings hold across k?

```{r probe-by-k}
# For each k: which topic do the mother and gender words fall into, and what is
# that topic about (its top 6 words)? If 母亲 stays with the family words at
# every k, the finding does not depend on the choice of k.
probe_by_k <- map_dfr(names(k_models), function(k) {
  m <- k_models[[k]]
  topic_words <- apply(seededlda::terms(m, 6), 2, paste, collapse = " ")
  landing(m, c("母亲", "树娟", "吕丽萍", "女人", "克夫")) %>%
    mutate(k = as.integer(k), topic_words = topic_words[top_topic]) %>%
    select(word, k, top_topic, p_top, topic_words)
}) %>%
  arrange(factor(word, levels = c("母亲", "树娟", "吕丽萍", "女人", "克夫")), k)
kable(probe_by_k)
write_excel_csv(probe_by_k, file.path(out_dir, "probe_words_by_k.csv"))
```

## Final unsupervised model

Topic models start from a random position, so two runs with different random
seeds give slightly different topics. (The same seed always gives exactly the
same result, so re-knitting never changes anything.) To avoid reporting a
lucky or unlucky run, the model is fitted 100 times and the **most typical
run** (the "medoid") is kept. Runs are compared on four criteria: the words
in each topic, the size of each topic, which paragraphs each topic is assigned
to, and the distances between topics (the layout of the LDAvis map). Each run
is ranked on each criterion by its average agreement with the other 99 runs,
and the run with the best average rank is used. See Roberts, Stewart and Tingley
(2016) on why topic models should be run from multiple starting points.

```{r lda}
# Change k_chosen after looking at the plots and word lists above.
k_chosen <- 8
n_runs <- 100     # number of restarts (100 gives about +/-10 points precision on "% of runs")

# Fit the unsupervised model 100 times with different random seeds
lda_runs <- map(1:n_runs, function(s) {
  set.seed(s)
  textmodel_lda(dfmat, k = k_chosen, max_iter = 2000, auto_iter = TRUE)
})

# Convergence check: each run stops early once it converges (auto_iter = TRUE).
# A run that used all 2000 iterations would not have converged.
iters <- unlist(lapply(lda_runs, function(m) m$last_iter))
if (length(iters)) cat("Gibbs iterations used per run: min", min(iters), ", max", max(iters),
                       "(limit 2000)\n")

# Compare all pairs of runs on four criteria and find the most typical run
typ_lda <- typical_run(lda_runs)
cat("How similar the runs are (1 = identical):\n")
kable(typ_lda$overall)
cat("The 5 most typical runs (rank 1 = most typical on that criterion):\n")
kable(head(typ_lda$table, 5))
write_excel_csv(typ_lda$table, file.path(out_dir, "stability_lda_runs.csv"))
lda_medoid <- typ_lda$medoid

# Report the most typical run
lda <- lda_runs[[lda_medoid]]
kable(seededlda::terms(lda, 12))

# Which topics of this run are stable across all runs?
lda_topic_stab <- topic_stability(lda_runs, lda_medoid)
kable(lda_topic_stab)
write_excel_csv(lda_topic_stab, file.path(out_dir, "stability_lda_topics.csv"))
```

```{r lda-export}
# Which topic each key word most likely belongs to (landing() is defined above)

                           "丈夫", "婚姻", "铁头", "继父", "命运", "文革"))
```

## Topic map (LDAvis) for the unsupervised model

The same interactive topic map as in section 12, drawn for the most typical
unsupervised run. Click this chunk's green arrow: the map opens in RStudio's
Viewer pane, and a summary table prints below the chunk. LDAvis numbers topics
by size (1 = largest), so the table shows which LDAvis number is which model
topic, with its size, its stability across the 100 runs, and its top 15 words.
Run `lda-export` first (it makes `lda_shares`).

```{r lda-ldavis}
# 1. The LDAvis data for the unsupervised model
json_lda <- createJSON(phi = lda$phi,
                       theta = lda$theta,
                       doc.length = rowSums(dfmat),
                       vocab = colnames(lda$phi),
                       term.frequency = colSums(dfmat)[colnames(lda$phi)])
serVis(json_lda, out.dir = file.path(out_dir, "LDAvis_unsupervised"), open.browser = FALSE)

# 2. One self-contained page (code, style and data in one file), as in section 12
vis_dir <- file.path(out_dir, "LDAvis_unsupervised")
read_vis <- function(f) paste(readLines(file.path(vis_dir, f), warn = FALSE,
                                        encoding = "UTF-8"), collapse = "\n")
lda_page <- paste0(
  '<!DOCTYPE html>\n<html><head><meta charset="utf-8">',
  '<title>LDAvis: Blue Kite unsupervised LDA</title>\n',
  '<style>', read_vis("lda.css"), '</style>\n',
  '<script>', read_vis("d3.v3.js"), '</script>\n',
  '<script>', read_vis("ldavis.js"), '</script>\n',
  '</head><body><div id="lda"></div>\n<script>\n',
  'var LDA_DATA = ', read_vis("lda.json"), ';\n',
  'd3.json = function(url, callback) { callback(null, LDA_DATA); };\n',
  'var vis = new LDAvis("#lda", "lda.json");\n',
  '</script></body></html>')
writeLines(lda_page, file.path(out_dir, "LDAvis_unsupervised_standalone.html"), useBytes = TRUE)

# 3. Summary table: LDAvis number -> model topic, size, stability, top 15 words
vis_order <- jsonlite::fromJSON(json_lda)$topic.order
top15 <- seededlda::terms(lda, 15)
lda_summary <- tibble(ldavis_number = seq_along(vis_order),
                      topic = rownames(lda$phi)[vis_order]) %>%
  left_join(lda_shares, by = "topic") %>%
  left_join(dplyr::select(lda_topic_stab, topic, mean_similarity, pct_runs_above_0.8),
            by = "topic") %>%

            by = "topic")

# 4. Show the map: in RStudio it opens in the Viewer pane (the Viewer only shows

#    when knitting, it is embedded in the report instead.

  file.copy(file.path(out_dir, "LDAvis_unsupervised_standalone.html"), tmp, overwrite = TRUE)
  viewer <- getOption("viewer")
  if (!is.null(viewer)) viewer(tmp) else utils::browseURL(tmp)
} else {
  htmltools::tags$iframe(srcdoc = lda_page, width = "100%", height = "900",
                         style = "border: 1px solid #ddd;")
}
```

# 9. Seeded LDA with clean seeds

The dictionary locked on October 16, 2026 (Appendix Table A3 in the paper).

- **Seed rule.** A word seeds a topic only if (1) it lands mainly in the
  matching unsupervised topic (section 8), (2) it appears in at least 10
  paragraphs, (3) it has one clear meaning, and (4) it does not interfere with
  the gender test. Political Campaigns and Gender have no unsupervised
  counterpart, so they are judged on (2) to (4).
- **Political Campaigns** has its own topic so that campaign vocabulary cannot
  be absorbed into the kinship topics.
- **Gender (test topic)** is seeded with sex-category words only (女人 男人
  女性). Marriage words, 克夫, the mother's names and the chapter titles are
  left unseeded; where they land is the result (sections 9 and 10).
- **The Party and the State was dropped.** Unsupervised topic 7 is the
  extended-family subplot, and the political words (政治 人民 主义 国家) land in
  Fate and the Era. Their placement is reported instead.
- 7 seeded topics + 3 residual topics (10 in total); section 11 varies the
  residual count and tests two alternative dictionaries.

```{r seeds}
# Seed words for each theme (each word appears in only one topic).
# Order follows Appendix Table A3: kinship, history, the film, then the test topic.
seeds <- dictionary(list(
  parents_child        = c("孩子", "儿子", "父亲"),
  political_campaigns  = c("文革", "运动", "右派", "反右", "批斗", "红卫兵",
                           "反革命", "大跃进", "整风", "劳改"),
  fate_era             = c("时代", "命运", "个人", "普通", "人性", "悲剧"),
  generational_memory  = c("过去", "反思", "年轻", "一代", "了解"),
  censorship_fifth_gen = c("导演", "田壮壮", "禁片", "被禁", "十年", "第五代",
                           "霸王别姬", "活着", "张艺谋", "陈凯歌"),
  film_form            = c("镜头", "叙事", "视角", "观众", "表达", "情感"),
  gender               = c("女人", "男人", "女性")
))
n_residual <- 3   # residual ("other") topics with no seeds

# Words deliberately NOT seeded, to see where the model puts them
probes <- c(
  # Shujuan / the mother, the narrator, and the chapter titles
  "母亲", "妈妈", "树娟", "吕丽萍", "铁头", "爸爸", "叔叔", "继父",
  # marriage words and 克夫 (outcome 3 of the gender test)
  "婚姻", "结婚", "改嫁", "嫁", "丈夫", "克夫",
  # words considered and dropped as seeds; their placement is reported
  "家庭", "历史", "记忆", "政治", "人民", "国家", "党", "革命", "角色",
  # symbols
  "乌鸦", "蓝色", "自由", "平静")

# Checks: no word in two topics, no probe seeded, and report seeds that are
# too rare to be in the vocabulary (they are simply ignored)
seed_words <- unlist(as.list(seeds), use.names = FALSE)
stopifnot(!any(duplicated(seed_words)), !any(probes %in% seed_words))
missing_seeds <- setdiff(seed_words, featnames(dfmat))
if (length(missing_seeds)) cat("Seed words not in the vocabulary (ignored):",
                               paste(missing_seeds, collapse = " "), "\n")

# Paragraphs containing each seed (for the Table A3 note; the rule is >= 10)
seed_counts <- tibble(topic = rep(names(seeds), lengths(as.list(seeds))),
                      word = seed_words,
                      paragraphs = as.integer(docfreq(dfmat)[seed_words]))
kable(seed_counts)
write_excel_csv(seed_counts, file.path(out_dir, "seed_paragraph_counts.csv"))
```

## Stability across 100 runs, and the most typical run

As with the unsupervised model, the seeded model is fitted 100 times. Seeded
topics have names, so runs are compared topic by topic. The tables below show
how much the results vary, and every table and figure after this section
(including LDAvis) uses the **most typical run**.

```{r stability-seeded}
# Fit: 7 seeded topics + 3 residual ("other") topics, 100 times
seeded_runs <- map(1:n_runs, function(s) {
  set.seed(s)
  textmodel_seededlda(dfmat, seeds, residual = n_residual, max_iter = 2000, auto_iter = TRUE)
})
seeded_names <- names(seeds)

# Convergence check (see the unsupervised model above)
iters <- unlist(lapply(seeded_runs, function(m) m$last_iter))
if (length(iters)) cat("Gibbs iterations used per run: min", min(iters), ", max", max(iters),
                       "(limit 2000)\n")

# Compare all pairs of runs on four criteria (seeded topics matched by name)
typ_s <- typical_run(seeded_runs, names = seeded_names)
cat("How similar the runs are (1 = identical):\n")
kable(typ_s$overall)
cat("The 5 most typical runs (rank 1 = most typical on that criterion):\n")
kable(head(typ_s$table, 5))
write_excel_csv(typ_s$table, file.path(out_dir, "stability_seeded_runs.csv"))
seeded_medoid <- typ_s$medoid

# (a) Topic sizes: average, smallest and largest share across all runs
share_summary <- map_dfr(seq_along(seeded_runs), function(i) {
  sh <- topic_share(seeded_runs[[i]])
  tibble(run = i, topic = names(sh), share = 100 * sh)
}) %>%
  group_by(topic) %>%
  summarise(mean_pct = round(mean(share), 1), min_pct = round(min(share), 1),
            max_pct = round(max(share), 1)) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_pct))
kable(share_summary)
write_excel_csv(share_summary, file.path(out_dir, "stability_topic_shares.csv"))

# (b) Where key words land: in how many runs each word falls in each topic
stab_words <- c("母亲", "妈妈", "树娟", "吕丽萍", "铁头", "继父",
                "婚姻", "嫁", "丈夫", "克夫", "政治", "历史")
landing_summary <- map_dfr(seq_along(seeded_runs),
                           ~ landing(seeded_runs[[.x]], stab_words) %>% mutate(run = .x)) %>%
  count(word, top_topic, name = "runs") %>%
  mutate(pct_runs = round(100 * runs / n_runs)) %>%
  arrange(factor(word, levels = stab_words), desc(runs))
kable(landing_summary)
write_excel_csv(landing_summary, file.path(out_dir, "stability_word_landing.csv"))

# (c) Stable top words: words in a topic's top 10 in at least 80% of runs
stable_words <- map_dfr(seq_along(seeded_runs), function(i) {
  tt <- seededlda::terms(seeded_runs[[i]], 10)
  tibble(run = i, topic = rep(colnames(tt), each = nrow(tt)), word = as.vector(tt))
}) %>%
  filter(topic %in% seeded_names) %>%
  count(topic, word) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / n_runs)) %>%
  filter(pct >= 80) %>%
  arrange(topic, desc(pct)) %>%
  group_by(topic) %>%
  summarise(stable_top_words = paste0(word, " (", pct, "%)", collapse = "  "))
kable(stable_words)
write_excel_csv(stable_words, file.path(out_dir, "stability_top_words.csv"))

# From here on, use the most typical run
slda <- seeded_runs[[seeded_medoid]]
kable(seededlda::terms(slda, 12))

# Which seeded topics are stable across all runs?
seeded_topic_stab <- topic_stability(seeded_runs, seeded_medoid, names = seeded_names)
kable(seeded_topic_stab)
write_excel_csv(seeded_topic_stab, file.path(out_dir, "stability_seeded_topics.csv"))
```

## Topic prevalence (share of tokens)

```{r prevalence}
# Share of all words in the corpus assigned to each topic (topic_share() is defined in section 8)
prev <- tibble(topic = names(topic_share(slda)),
               share_pct = round(100 * topic_share(slda), 1))
kable(prev)
write_excel_csv(prev, file.path(out_dir, "seeded_topic_prevalence.csv"))
```

## Topic shares aggregated to reviews

```{r review-level}
# Each review contributes several paragraphs; here paragraph topic shares are
# combined back into one profile per review (weighted by paragraph length).
para_len <- rowSums(dfmat)
review_id <- docvars(dfmat, "id")
review_theta <- rowsum(slda$theta * para_len, review_id) / as.vector(rowsum(para_len, review_id))

review_level <- tibble(topic = colnames(review_theta),
                       mean_share_pct = round(100 * colMeans(review_theta), 1),
                       pct_reviews_with_20pct_plus = round(100 * colMeans(review_theta >= 0.2), 1)) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_share_pct))
kable(review_level)
write_excel_csv(review_level, file.path(out_dir, "seeded_topic_by_review.csv"))
```

## The gender test

The outcomes, stated before the results: if the Gender topic fills with era,
nation and campaign words (or sits close to Political Campaigns and Fate and
the Era), viewers read the woman as the bearer of national history; if it
fills with subjectivity words, they share the critics' frame; if it fills with
mother, family, fate, 克夫 or marriage words, they use a frame of their own; if
it does not hold together across runs, the reviews have no organized gender
discussion. Stability across runs is in `stability_seeded_topics.csv`.

```{r gender-test}
# 1. How much of the Gender topic is its own seeds? Share of the topic's word
#    probability that comes from 女人 男人 女性. Near 1 = little more than its
#    seeds; lower = it attracts other vocabulary.
g_seeds <- intersect(as.list(seeds)$gender, colnames(slda$phi))
g_share <- round(sum(slda$phi["gender", g_seeds]), 2)
cat("Share of the Gender topic's probability from its seeds:", g_share, "\n")
write_excel_csv(tibble(seeds = paste(g_seeds, collapse = " "), seed_share = g_share),
                file.path(out_dir, "gender_seed_share.csv"))

# 2. What fills it: top 30 words by probability (lambda = 1) and by relevance
#    (lambda = 0.6, as in LDAvis). Seeds are marked with *.
relevance_terms <- function(m, topic, lambda, n = 30, x = dfmat) {
  pw <- colSums(x)[colnames(m$phi)]
  pw <- pw / sum(pw)
  r <- lambda * log(m$phi[topic, ]) + (1 - lambda) * log(m$phi[topic, ] / pw)
  names(sort(r, decreasing = TRUE))[1:n]
}
mark_seed <- function(w) ifelse(w %in% g_seeds, paste0(w, "*"), w)
gender_words <- tibble(rank = 1:30,
                       by_probability = mark_seed(relevance_terms(slda, "gender", 1)),
                       by_relevance_0.6 = mark_seed(relevance_terms(slda, "gender", 0.6)))
kable(gender_words)
write_excel_csv(gender_words, file.path(out_dir, "gender_topic_words.csv"))

# 3. Where the Gender topic sits. Campaign words are seeded elsewhere, so
#    outcome 1 is read from closeness to political_campaigns and fate_era:
#    (a) distance between word distributions (Jensen-Shannon, as in LDAvis;
#        smaller = more similar), (b) correlation of paragraph shares
#        (positive = discussed in the same paragraphs).
others <- setdiff(rownames(slda$phi), "gender")
gender_rel <- tibble(
  topic = others,
  js_distance = round(map_dbl(others, ~ js_div(slda$phi["gender", ], slda$phi[.x, ])), 3),
  theta_cor = round(map_dbl(others, ~ cor(slda$theta[, "gender"], slda$theta[, .x])), 2)) %>%
  arrange(js_distance)
kable(gender_rel)
write_excel_csv(gender_rel, file.path(out_dir, "gender_topic_relations.csv"))

# 4. The 30 paragraphs with the highest Gender share, for close reading
top_g <- order(slda$theta[, "gender"], decreasing = TRUE)[1:30]
gender_paras <- tibble(doc_id = docnames(dfmat)[top_g],
                       gender_share = round(slda$theta[top_g, "gender"], 2)) %>%
  left_join(paras %>% select(doc_id, date, votes, text), by = "doc_id")
write_excel_csv(gender_paras, file.path(out_dir, "gender_top_paragraphs.csv"))
```

# 10. Where do the mother and other key words land?

For each word, the probability of each topic given that word
(p(topic | word), from the model's word distributions weighted by topic size).

```{r probes}
# For each word: which topic is it most likely to belong to? (landing() is defined in section 8)
check_words <- unique(c(probes, "女人", "男人", "女性", "命运", "文革"))
land <- landing(slda, check_words)
kable(land)
write_excel_csv(land, file.path(out_dir, "probe_word_topics.csv"))
```

# 11. Robustness

## Different random starts and residual topics

Does the mother still land in the same topic, and does the Gender topic keep
the same size, when the model is rerun?

```{r robustness}
# 9 reruns: 3 random seeds x 1, 2 or 3 residual topics
runs <- expand_grid(seed = c(1, 42, 2025), residual = c(1, 2, 3))
robust <- pmap_dfr(runs, function(seed, residual) {
  set.seed(seed)
  m <- textmodel_seededlda(dfmat, seeds, residual = residual,
                           max_iter = 2000, auto_iter = TRUE)
  sh <- topic_share(m)
  l <- landing(m, c("母亲", "树娟", "丈夫", "婚姻", "克夫"))
  lands <- function(w) if (w %in% l$word) l$top_topic[l$word == w] else NA
  tibble(seed = seed, residual = residual,
         gender_pct = round(100 * sh[["gender"]], 1),
         parents_child_pct = round(100 * sh[["parents_child"]], 1),
         mother_lands_in = lands("母亲"),
         shujuan_lands_in = lands("树娟"),
         husband_lands_in = lands("丈夫"),
         marriage_lands_in = lands("婚姻"),
         kefu_lands_in = lands("克夫"))
})
kable(robust)
write_excel_csv(robust, file.path(out_dir, "robustness.csv"))
```

## Alternative dictionaries

Two checks on the design, each fitted once (seed 2025, 3 residual topics):

- **(a) Bundled women and marriage.** The earlier design: the Gender seeds
  plus the marriage words and 克夫 in one topic. Shows whether the result
  depends on keeping gender and marriage apart.
- **(b) Chapter titles seeded.** 爸爸, 叔叔 and 继父 added to Parents and Child.
  Shows whether the mother and the marriage words move when the husbands are
  fixed as fathers.

```{r robustness-alt}
alt_dicts <- list(
  a_women_marriage = local({
    d <- as.list(seeds)
    d$gender <- NULL
    d$women_marriage <- c("女人", "男人", "女性", "婚姻", "结婚", "改嫁", "嫁", "丈夫", "克夫")
    dictionary(d)
  }),
  b_titles_seeded = local({
    d <- as.list(seeds)
    d$parents_child <- c(d$parents_child, "爸爸", "叔叔", "继父")
    dictionary(d)
  })
)
alt_words <- c("母亲", "妈妈", "树娟", "铁头", "女人", "丈夫", "婚姻", "克夫", "政治")
alt_terms <- list()
alt_results <- imap_dfr(alt_dicts, function(d, nm) {
  set.seed(2025)
  m <- textmodel_seededlda(dfmat, d, residual = n_residual,
                           max_iter = 2000, auto_iter = TRUE)
  test_topic <- intersect(c("women_marriage", "gender"), rownames(m$phi))[1]
  top15 <- paste(seededlda::terms(m, 15)[, test_topic], collapse = " ")
  cat("\n", nm, ": top 15 words of", test_topic, "\n", top15, "\n")
  alt_terms[[nm]] <<- tibble(dictionary = nm, test_topic = test_topic, top15_words = top15)
  landing(m, alt_words) %>%
    mutate(dictionary = nm, test_topic_pct = round(100 * topic_share(m)[[test_topic]], 1))
})
kable(alt_results)
write_excel_csv(alt_results, file.path(out_dir, "robustness_alt_dictionaries.csv"))
write_excel_csv(bind_rows(alt_terms), file.path(out_dir, "robustness_alt_test_topic_words.csv"))
```

## Whole reviews instead of paragraphs

The same seeded model fitted on the 306 whole reviews. If the main patterns
hold here too, they do not depend on splitting reviews into paragraphs.

```{r whole-review}
# Add each review's paragraphs back together into one document per review
dfm_review <- dfm_group(dfmat, groups = docvars(dfmat, "id"))

set.seed(2025)
slda_review <- textmodel_seededlda(dfm_review, seeds, residual = n_residual,
                                   max_iter = 2000, auto_iter = TRUE)
kable(seededlda::terms(slda_review, 10))
write_excel_csv(as_tibble(seededlda::terms(slda_review, 15)), file.path(out_dir, "review_model_terms.csv"))

# Compare: where key words land in the review-level vs paragraph-level model
compare <- landing(slda_review, check_words, x = dfm_review) %>%
  select(word, review_model = top_topic, review_p = p_top) %>%
  left_join(land %>% select(word, paragraph_model = top_topic, paragraph_p = p_top),
            by = "word")
kable(compare)
write_excel_csv(compare, file.path(out_dir, "review_vs_paragraph_model.csv"))
```

# 12. LDAvis

Three ways to see the topic map:

- **In this report:** it is embedded below (scroll inside the frame).
- **In RStudio's Viewer pane:** run the `ldavis-viewer` chunk with its green
  arrow. It only reads the saved file, so it opens instantly without rerunning
  the models.
- **In your browser:** double-click `LDAvis_seeded_standalone.html` in this
  run's folder. (The `index.html` inside its `LDAvis_seeded/` folder will look blank if opened
  directly, because browsers block it from loading its data file.)

LDAvis renumbers topics by size, so the table below maps its numbers to the
topic names.

```{r ldavis}
# Build the LDAvis data from the seeded model
json <- createJSON(phi = slda$phi,
                   theta = slda$theta,
                   doc.length = rowSums(dfmat),
                   vocab = colnames(slda$phi),
                   term.frequency = colSums(dfmat)[colnames(slda$phi)])
write(json, file.path(out_dir, "ldavis_seeded.json"))              # same format your Shiny app reads
serVis(json, out.dir = file.path(out_dir, "LDAvis_seeded"), open.browser = FALSE)

# Make a single self-contained page: put the code, style and data inside one
# HTML file, and point LDAvis at the embedded data instead of a separate file.
ldavis_dir <- file.path(out_dir, "LDAvis_seeded")
read_txt <- function(f) paste(readLines(file.path(ldavis_dir, f), warn = FALSE,
                                        encoding = "UTF-8"), collapse = "\n")
standalone <- paste0(
  '<!DOCTYPE html>\n<html><head><meta charset="utf-8">',
  '<title>LDAvis: Blue Kite seeded LDA</title>\n',
  '<style>', read_txt("lda.css"), '</style>\n',
  '<script>', read_txt("d3.v3.js"), '</script>\n',
  '<script>', read_txt("ldavis.js"), '</script>\n',
  '</head><body><div id="lda"></div>\n<script>\n',
  'var LDA_DATA = ', read_txt("lda.json"), ';\n',
  'd3.json = function(url, callback) { callback(null, LDA_DATA); };\n',
  'var vis = new LDAvis("#lda", "lda.json");\n',
  '</script></body></html>')
writeLines(standalone, file.path(out_dir, "LDAvis_seeded_standalone.html"), useBytes = TRUE)

# Which LDAvis number is which topic
topic_order <- jsonlite::fromJSON(json)$topic.order
kable(tibble(ldavis_topic = seq_along(topic_order),
             topic_name = rownames(slda$phi)[topic_order]))

# Embed the topic map in the knitted report. "srcdoc" puts the whole page inside
# the frame, so it does not depend on any other file.
htmltools::tags$iframe(srcdoc = standalone, width = "100%", height = "900",
                       style = "border: 1px solid #ddd;")
```

```{r ldavis-viewer}
# Open the saved topic map in RStudio's Viewer pane.
# Run this chunk with its green arrow; during Knit it does nothing.
# RStudio's Viewer only shows local pages from R's temporary folder, so the
# file is copied there first. Outside RStudio it opens in your browser instead.
if (interactive()) {
  # If this chunk is run on its own in a fresh session, use the latest run folder
  if (!exists("out_dir")) {
    out_dir <- tail(sort(grep("/run_", list.dirs("r_output", recursive = FALSE), value = TRUE)), 1)
  }
  src <- file.path(out_dir, "LDAvis_seeded_standalone.html")
  tmp <- file.path(tempdir(), "LDAvis_seeded_standalone.html")
  file.copy(src, tmp, overwrite = TRUE)
  viewer <- getOption("viewer")
  if (!is.null(viewer)) viewer(tmp) else utils::browseURL(tmp)
}
```
